# Finite transparent guard completeness — candidate revision 1

Parent: GVG-GUARD-COMPLETE-1, under GUARD-INTERACTION-THEORY-20261025/r1.
Status: constructive Lean candidate, NOT_CHECKED and NOT_REVIEWED by this author.
Author: /root/finite_guard_completeness_astra_r1; requested gpt-6-astra/medium;
observed model/effort UNKNOWN. No coauthors or descendants at author freeze.
No production authority or native correspondence is claimed.

## Original claim and actual construction

For every n and every existing GuardedValueGraph.FiniteGraph n, the sole traversed
edge is the existing Node.next. No additional property of the graph or node
bodies is assumed by walk or decideGuard. The constructor domain is exactly the
accepted unit/pair/lam/delay/alias/view/roll/evidence research domain. In particular,
roll/view/evidence remain identity-typed in this model; this does not prove the
paper's type-changing forms.

walkAux structurally recurses on fuel. It carries a duplicate-free list seen,
seen.length + fuel = n, and a nonempty transparent path from each saved vertex
to the current vertex. Membership immediately supplies an actual cycle. For a
new vertex, Node.next = none returns that vertex, a terminality proof, exact
distance and Observes proof. A successor consumes one fuel unit and extends all
saved paths by the actual edge. At zero fuel a new vertex would give a
nodup list of n+1 members of Fin n, contradicting the constructive finite-list
bound. Thus this branch is impossible for the supplied invariants; it is not an
assumed traversal-termination fact. The cycle branch also carries Reaches from
the requested root, so a tail entering a cycle is covered.

The terminal distance is strictly less than n. height g n r computes a natural
number solely by n iterations of actual Node.next. ends_height identifies it
with the exact terminal distance once enough fuel is available. The endpoint
and distance supplied by walk derive AllEnd from NoCycle, then guardOfAllEnd
constructs rank = height g n, ceiling = n, the strict bound and strict descent
on every actual transparent edge. Its AllEnd premise is discharged by
allEnd_of_noCycle; no rank existence, chosen minimum, choice, well-foundedness
oracle or assumed termination enters the main result.

guarded_iff_noCycle combines guardOfNoCycle with the accepted
no_transparent_cycle converse. scan runs walk on the explicit List.finRange n;
decideGuard returns a computed Guarded certificate or a concrete vertex and
nonempty TransparentPath cycle. noCycleDecidable packages the same executable
case split. The empty graph needs no arbitrary starting vertex. Each root walk
uses at most n successor inspections and n+1 membership checks; scan repeats
this finite computation over n roots. This is a simple research decision,
without a native efficiency claim or benchmark.

## Application to original graph and rec extension

finite_reference_canonical and finite_no_bottom apply the constructed certificate
to the accepted canonical-observation and bottom-exclusion lemmas immediately.
Their only graph hypotheses are the original WellTyped assignment and NoCycle.

freshGraph keeps exactly those fresh Node.next edges whose target is Sum.inr;
none and old targets are terminal only for this local analysis. freshGraph_edge
proves the exact equivalence to the original fresh node's successor equation.
fresh_path_allocation transports the resulting nonempty paths to actual
allocate nodes. This makes the local criterion auditable against its constructor,
not an independently assumed transition system.

allocateFiniteGuard derives local rank, ceiling, bound and decrease from
FreshNoCycle and feeds them to the accepted allocate_guard. It allows all
fresh-to-old edges and retains the original old certificate. allocate_guard_iff
also proves necessity of the local cycle criterion under that old certificate.
finite_rec_extension supplies the original conjunction: post-allocation graph
typing, typed canonical observation of every old/new reference, and the typed
simultaneously closed body. The original old typing, per-fresh-node typing and
body typing premises remain intact. finite_rec_extension_from_cycles removes
the old supplied certificate too when the old graph is finite.

This is an application to the parent mathematical obstruction, not another
assumed-rank theorem. Subject to successful elaboration and fresh independent
review, it supplies the exact missing finite-rank completeness direction.
Luna alone adjudicates that local gate. Full-paper and native parent gates remain
OPEN regardless of the local result.

## Falsifiers and boundaries

The Lean candidate includes the following concrete constructions and quantified
proofs, not executed tests:

- zeroGraph and zeroGraph_guard handle n=0; decideGuard itself scans an empty list.
- countdown n has n+1 vertices and a maximal n-edge transparent chain.
  countdown_ends and countdown_exact_height establish its exact distance for
  every vertex; no off-by-one escape is assumed.
- selfCycle_rejected excludes a transparent self-alias.
- cycleWithTail has 0→1→2→2; tail_reaches_cycle, tail_cycle_explicit and
  tail_cycle_rejected expose both the tail and the nonempty cycle.
- sharedTerminal has two aliases reaching the same terminal; its certificate is
  obtained from constructed endpoint proofs.
- finiteMutualLambda contains two actual lambda bodies calling the opposite
  reference; its node typing and NoCycle are constructed. This permits recursive
  computation and makes no claim that evaluation terminates.
- dataSelfCycle passes the outer guard test because pair fields are genuine
  guards. No impossible finite recursive Ty equation or node-typing derivation
  is claimed for that self-pair.
- oldAliasFresh and oldAliasAllocation_guard allow a new alias to any old node,
  including an old reference domain that is not finite.

The universal proofs cover every mixed alias/view/roll/evidence chain and cycle,
all concrete data/code nodes, sharing, graph size zero and arbitrary finite size.
No whole-graph DAG condition is introduced. The list bound is reproved with
explicit DecidableEq because the general library Nodup.length_le_of_subset
proof uses classical equality. Library source for the used Fin/list/erase
lemmas was inspected; the primary must still inspect the full emitted axiom
closure. No sorry, new axiom, Classical.choice or native_decide is used in the
candidate source.

## Reuse and remaining owners

Reused only within accepted premises: GuardedValueGraph.no_transparent_cycle,
reference_canonical, no_bottom_reference, allocate_guard, allocate_typed and
closeBody_typed. The old rank-based rec_extension remains immutable; the new
finite theorem supplies its missing rank inputs instead of changing semantics.
The paper's graph-extension/value-form passages motivate the parent but do not
supply machine-checked full-paper RHS or type-changing-form premises. No prior
failed construction is revived, and no historical result is generalized by
analogy. No actual compiler/native source audit is claimed.

FGD-CHECK-1 — Luna owns primary elaboration, dependency/axiom inspection, repairs
only after acknowledged author STOP and fresh nonauthor review. Falsifier: any
elaboration failure, forbidden axiom, or finite graph for which the produced
terminal/cycle witness or strict rank equation is invalid. The exact source
suppliers are walkAux/height/freshGraph; consumers are guardOfNoCycle,
allocateFiniteGuard and finite_rec_extension. No production edit is needed.

GVG-FORMS-1 — full-paper graph proof owner: actual mu, type-changing roll/views,
type evidence and missing eliminators. Falsifier: transparent traversal preserves
this model's type but fails the real eliminator's required evidence.
GVG-REC-RHS-1 — full-paper syntax/binder owner: derive fresh NodeTyped premises
from full original rec RHS derivations under all actual binders. Existing Term
substitution covers its own five-constructor domain only.
ENV-GRAPH-1 — Luna/source intake: native graph realization from current cells,
initialization/preallocation and machine.rs Instruction::Lambda,
Frame::ValueEntry, Machine::lookup/extend and Callee, plus receiving.rs lambda
schema construction. Current graph mathematics does not establish those source
constructors emit this representation or satisfy its typing/cycle conditions.
Original F1/FK1, foreign continuations, Simple-sub generation/accumulation/

# Higher-order repeated interaction value safety

Status: candidate mathematics; author has NOT_RUN Lean, tests or builds. Fresh
independent review and primary elaboration are pending. No production authority.
Author: `/root/higher_order_interaction_astra_r1`, requested `gpt-6-astra/medium`,
observed model/effort UNKNOWN. No descendants or other contributing authors at
this author freeze. Any primary repair after acknowledged STOP adds coauthorship.
Contract: `GUARD-INTERACTION-THEORY-20261025/r1`, lane B, HO-INTERACTION-1.
Baseline: `e9c0a89d2f92ac0116a75e5c7e24623e4c38acd9` (supplied; no Git invoked).

## Original parent and exact contribution

The original parent is the execution type-safety theorem in
`docs/yulang-operational-type-safety-ja.tex:1139`–1159. It quantifies over every
finite prefix of internal transitions, typed external responses and multiple
resumptions, allowing stopping at a request; returned callback code is typed.
Its graph extension and metadata clauses remain part of that original claim.
The request-cut lemma at 1047–1066 and raw resume discussion at 458–472 are the
precise supporting parent obligations. They are research targets, not adopted
compiler semantics.

The new module `lean/YulangClosure/HigherOrderInteraction.lean` supplies a
candidate repeated-interaction proof for the accepted finite HigherOrder
research grammar. The response, saved handle, outer evaluation context and
finite trace are independently quantified. It extends the accepted internal
trace safety construction with real request capture and arbitrary old-handle
responses. It does not substitute one lambda frame action for F1/FK1 or identify
this value-typing projection with the paper's complete raw Resume operation.

`closed_program_interaction_safety` starts with only a closed typed computation
and an EMPTY saved arena. `finite_saved_response_safety` applies the result to
ANY entry captured during ANY such finite trace and ANY closed response having
that entry's own operation response type. It supplies actual publication
provenance, the original result type, all saved-entry typing, and resumed
progress. Thus captured continuation typing is not an assumed initial resource.

## Raw construction and proof chain

`Saved` retains the full operation instance, exact payload, original
response-binding continuation and entire `Safety.EvalContext`. Its fields carry
no typing derivations. An arena is a finite list. Handles are natural-number
positions; publication appends at the old length. `lookup_append_old`,
`lookup_append_fresh` and `lookup_length_none` establish stable old entries and a
fresh position. No allocation or response mutates any old saved record.

`RawStep.internal` embeds the accepted `Safety.Step`; `RawStep.publish` matches
only a current computation that IS the saved context plugged with that exact
request; `RawStep.response` looks up an existing handle and substitutes the
provided raw value into its original response binder before plugging the entire
saved context. Response is permitted from any phase and any old handle, so an
external scheduler can revisit saved continuations in any order. No raw rule
contains typing, preservation, or a protocol premise. This is an abstract
interaction scheduler, not a claim about native API authentication or scheduling.

`Protocol` is separate. Internal and publication events impose no external
obligation. A response must identify the FULL saved operation instance and have
its exact response type under the empty context. Full-instance equality retains
operation identity, ordered type arguments, payload type and response type;
equality of merely the last type is insufficient. The protocol never postulates
that a response exists. In particular a bottom response type can legitimately
leave the execution waiting forever.

`capture_typed` inverts the actual current computation with
`Safety.context_inversion`, then inverts `CompTyped.request`. This derives exact
payload typing, the continuation under the operation's response binder, and
`ContextTyped` for the whole enclosing context. `saved_resume_typed` uses the
accepted substitution theorem and `plug_typed` on those derived witnesses.
`step_preservation` applies this at publication, preserves all old entries, and
uses independently supplied response typing only at response steps.

`Trace` combines raw steps with the explicit external protocol, without adding a
preservation premise. `finite_interaction_safety` proves the same result type,
ALL saved-entry typings, concrete progress, and exact equality of all initially
saved entries after EVERY finite trace. `trace_origin` additionally shows that
each final entry either existed initially or has an exact publish event at that
handle in the trace. `initial_saved_origin` eliminates the initial-data case.
`typed_response_association` combines the saved payload and continuation facts
with the externally supplied instance and response typing.

`Progress` has precisely four forms: a running Ret, a running failure at a
finite evaluation-context hole, a wait at an existing exact saved request, or
an actual protocol-respecting next step. It has no arbitrary-stuck constructor.
`plug_suspended` and `publication_has_no_internal_step` show that publication
comes from a genuine suspended evaluation position. `state_progress` derives
publication when the accepted closed-progress theorem exposes a request.
No response availability or fairness is required for progress at a wait.

## Distinguishing constructions

All rows below are Lean statements/proofs in the candidate, pending checking.
They are not claims that a native constructor generated the modeled transitions.

| Case | Candidate evidence |
| --- | --- |
| Every finite repetition at the same handle | `repeat_handle`, arbitrary list of independently typed values |
| Different handles in arbitrary order | `handles_in_any_order`; both handles/values independent, revisits the first |
| Old handle after a later capture | `capture_then_old_response`, using append preservation |
| Two distinct responses to one capture | `two_distinct_responses`, false then true; `two_response_safety` applies the parent invariant |
| Another request after resume | `new_request_after_resume`, five real interaction events with two further publications and reuse of handle zero |
| Higher-order response with typed code | `callable_response_trace`, `callable_response_typed`, `callable_response_can_progress` |
| Same types, wrong operation identity | `wrong_operation_example`, plus general `wrong_instance_rejected` |
| Missing handle | `missing_handle_rejected` |
| Uninhabited response type | `bottom_wait_trace`, `bottom_wait_safety`, `bottom_wait_no_response` |
| Retained bind/scope/expose context | `nested_request_typed`, `nested_resume_equation` |
| Exact arena immutability | `step_immutable`, `trace_immutable` |
| Actual capture provenance | `step_origin`, `trace_origin`, `initial_saved_origin` |

## Reuse, source boundary and remaining obligations

The accepted HigherOrderSyntax grammar and typing are unchanged. The accepted
HigherOrderSubstitution binder lifting and `substitute_top` are reused only for
that grammar. HigherOrderEntry supplies its already accepted lambda/wrap entry
constructions; HigherOrderSafety supplies all internal constructor preservation,
closed progress, actual evaluation contexts, context inversion and plugging.
Its old internal-only trace theorem is not reused as though it already included
external responses. The new Trace induction fills that specific gap.

Formal producer-to-consumer evidence is explicit:
`Comp.request` / `CompTyped.request` -> `Saved.request` / `RawStep.publish` ->
append-only arena lookup -> `RawStep.response` / `Saved.resume` ->
`substitute_top` / `EvalContext.plug` -> accepted internal execution. This is a
source-to-construction correspondence within the finite research syntax only.
There is no new inference constraint-generation/accumulation/propagation claim
and no native audit. Simple-sub levels, extrusion, qualifying intrusion,
generalization and every ordinary inference path remain outside this change.
No withdrawn bypass or residual/provider/witness collapse is introduced.

The original paper theorem remains OPEN for graph-bearing responses and fresh
immutable graph extensions, handlers and their arms, mapop, and the paper's Wait
constructor and forwarding frames. `Interaction.Phase.waiting` merely records
an exposed request; it does not implement that omitted language constructor.
The current `HigherOrderSyntax.Comp` and `Safety.EvalContext` lack those forms;
Luna owns any future syntax allocation and their preservation/progress proofs.

Owner/view freshening, live metadata interpretation, effect hygiene, linearity,
full F1/FK1 and native operation/response authenticity remain OPEN. This module
preserves metadata as existing immutable syntax and does not rename saved scope
owners for a fresh resume. Those clauses belong to the paper's full Resume/view
and graph semantics and require independent construction and authority; they
cannot follow from a value-typing theorem. The prior source inventory
`2026-10-25-higher-order-source-constructor-map.md` remains the native/source
ownership locator. Native entry, capture, dispatch and response owners were not
audited by this assignment. No new code TODO is justified without that evidence.

The exact next in-contract step belongs to Luna: elaborate the frozen module,
inspect theorem signatures/axioms and distinguishing constructions, acknowledge
any author-to-primary repair transfer, then appoint a fresh nonauthor reviewer.
The author cannot certify this candidate. No compiler/test or shared-record edit
is requested. A future expanded full-paper lane requires a new exact allocation.

# Higher-order research core and structural embedding

Status: Draft research construction; checking and review evidence is recorded in
the sprint outcome and its frozen receipts. This is not production authority.
Scope: frozen LEAN-HIGHER-ORDER-PROOF-CORE-20261025/r1 research representation.
Initial author: /root/higher_order_proof_core_astra_r1; requested gpt-6-astra/medium,
observed model/effort UNKNOWN. Primary /root repairs and integrates after author
STOP; the outcome records final authorship and independent review. No descendants.
Production authority: none. The operational paper is a proposal/target; the
2026-10-07 complete-Call definition §1 records permission for legitimate research
definitions, not adoption of this representation as compiler architecture.

The parent RESPONSE-ENCODING-1 / ENV-CALLABLE-1 lacked a callable constructor in
its formal Value sort. The candidate removes that specific representational
obstruction by constructing a new callable type and actual lambda/wrap values.
Every Original.Val/Comp and TypedCall.Value/Comp/Adapter/Function constructor is
mapped structurally. No old term is retained behind an opaque original opcode.
The full parent, native readback and operational safety remain OPEN.

## Syntax and quantifiers

`HigherOrderSyntax.lean` retains every old type constructor, all eight literal
domains and their exact payload representations, variables, delay, injections,
single-child intersection/top values and all seven Original computations. It
adds the existing Call view/scope/expose/request/fail nodes, lambda/wrap values,
and dynamicCall. Request's continuation binds its operation instance's response
type. The type language can place callable types beneath thunk/union/intersection
and in operation instances. The value, computation and adapter syntax is mutually
inductive; all typing judgments are defined afterwards.

Value-entry lambda binds A; computation-entry lambda binds Thunk A. Both retain
receipt, annotated input/body/result types, body and result consumer. Wrap keeps
the input adapter c→a and output adapter b→d around an a→b function. DynamicCall
accepts a thunk carrier. This fixes a research typing interface without asserting
an execution rule or operational equivalence for the new constructor.

`ContextEmbedding old new` quantifies over every old lookup fact. The mutual
Original and TypedCall preservation proofs quantify over arbitrary old terms,
old typing derivations and target contexts satisfying that relation. Closed
Original nodes embed under any target context using the empty lookup relation;
binders use `extend_embedding`. The Function theorem quantifies over every old
FunctionTyped derivation and every target context. No original constructor,
source-domain restriction or independent continuation quantifier is discarded.
This is one-way typing preservation, not reflection or full conservativity.

## Metadata boundary

Paths retain component lists, port kinds and translated endpoint types;
occurrences retain identities and paths. Operation instances retain operation
identity, ordered type arguments and both payload/response types. Receipt slots
and profiles retain order, identity and typed paths. Adapter metadata retains
all path correspondences and captured occurrences. Interface-port metadata also
has a structural map.

PathRule is a Prop in the accepted input. `embedPathRule` translates its proof
into a new Prop proof. It does not eliminate that proof into a data-valued map
identity. In particular the old permissive adapterMap rule remains permissive;
this work cannot prove that a mappingIdentity absent from runtime data can be
reconstructed. Syntax is **typing-proof-free**, not entirely proof-free. The old
Adapter.typed field is omitted from syntax and consumed solely to construct the
new extrinsic AdapterTyped derivation. The retained PathRule metadata neither
contains a typing judgment nor creates a typing-definition cycle.

## Parent application

`embedFunction_typed` constructs a ValueTyped callable from an old FunctionTyped
proof. `function_as_argument` and `call_with_function_argument` use it in the
actual new delayed argument and dynamicCall constructors.
`request_callable_response` constructs a request that binds and returns a

accepted `realized_substitution_typed` supplier to each represented context index;

construction before embedding. Both keep successful realization and CellsTyped
as explicit original premises. Nothing claims that arbitrary native closures
already satisfy those premises, or that old stores already represent new
callable values. Generic new callable storage and old represented-read transport
are two separate constructions whose native connection is still open.

import YulangClosure.GuardedValueGraph
import Init.Data.List.FinRange
import Init.Data.List.Erase

/-! Constructive finite transparent-graph decision. Research syntax only.
No rank, termination oracle, classical choice, or whole-graph acyclicity is input. -/
namespace YulangClosure.GuardedValueGraph.FiniteDecision

/-- Exact number of transparent edges before a concrete terminal node. -/
inductive Ends (g : Graph R) : R → Nat → Prop where
  | done (r) : (g r).next = none → Ends g r 0
  | step : (g r).next = some s → Ends g s k → Ends g r (k + 1)

def height (g : Graph R) : Nat → R → Nat
  | 0, _ => 0
  | fuel + 1, r => match (g r).next with
    | none => 0
    | some s => height g fuel s + 1

theorem ends_height {g : Graph R} {r : R} {k : Nat} (h : Ends g r k) :
    ∀ fuel, k ≤ fuel → height g fuel r = k := by
  induction h with
  | done r hn =>
      intro fuel _
      cases fuel <;> simp [height, hn]
  | @step r s k hs he ih =>
      intro fuel hk
      cases fuel with
      | zero => omega
      | succ fuel =>
          simp only [height, hs]
          rw [ih fuel (by omega)]

theorem ends_observes {g : Graph R} {r : R} {k : Nat} (h : Ends g r k) :
    ∃ node, Observes g r node := by
  induction h with
  | done r hn => exact ⟨g r, .done r hn⟩
  | step hs _ ih =>
      obtain ⟨node, ho⟩ := ih
      exact ⟨node, .step hs ho⟩

theorem path_trans {g : Graph R} {r s t : R}
    (h : TransparentPath g r s) (h' : TransparentPath g s t) :
    TransparentPath g r t := by
  induction h with
  | edge hs => exact .cons hs h'
  | cons hs _ ih => exact .cons hs (ih h')

/-- Delete one occurrence using the supplied decidable equality. The local
lemmas avoid classical dependencies in the library erase equivalences. -/
def eraseOne [DecidableEq A] (a : A) : List A → List A
  | [] => []
  | b :: bs => if b = a then bs else b :: eraseOne a bs

theorem eraseOne_mem [DecidableEq A] {a x : A} {ys : List A}
    (hne : x ≠ a) (hx : x ∈ ys) : x ∈ eraseOne a ys := by
  induction ys with
  | nil => cases hx
  | cons b bs ih =>
      by_cases h : b = a
      · simp only [eraseOne, h, if_true]
        rcases List.mem_cons.mp hx with he | ht
        · exact False.elim (hne (he.trans h))
        · exact ht
      · simp only [eraseOne, h, if_false]
        rcases List.mem_cons.mp hx with he | ht
        · exact List.mem_cons.mpr (.inl he)
        · exact List.mem_cons.mpr (.inr (ih ht))

theorem eraseOne_length [DecidableEq A] {a : A} {ys : List A}
    (ha : a ∈ ys) : (eraseOne a ys).length + 1 = ys.length := by
  induction ys with
  | nil => cases ha
  | cons b bs ih =>
      by_cases h : b = a
      · simp only [eraseOne, h, if_true, List.length_cons]
      · have ht : a ∈ bs := by
          rcases List.mem_cons.mp ha with he | ht
          · exact False.elim (h he.symm)
          · exact ht
        simp only [eraseOne, h, if_false, List.length_cons]
        have hi := ih ht
        omega

/-- Constructive finite-list bound, with no imported erase equivalence. -/
theorem nodup_length_le [DecidableEq A] {xs ys : List A}
    (hd : xs.Nodup) (hs : xs ⊆ ys) : xs.length ≤ ys.length := by
  induction xs generalizing ys with
  | nil => exact Nat.zero_le _
  | cons a xs ih =>
      rw [List.nodup_cons] at hd
      have ha : a ∈ ys := hs (List.mem_cons_self ..)
      have hsub : xs ⊆ eraseOne a ys := by
        intro x hx
        have hxa : x ≠ a := fun h => hd.1 (h ▸ hx)
        exact eraseOne_mem hxa (hs (List.mem_cons_of_mem _ hx))
      have hi := ih hd.2 hsub
      have hl := eraseOne_length ha
      simp only [List.length_cons]
      omega

theorem finite_list_bound {xs : List (Fin n)} (hd : xs.Nodup) :
    xs.length ≤ n := by
  have h := nodup_length_le (ys := List.finRange n) hd
    (fun x _ => List.mem_finRange x)
  simpa using h

/-- A finite, possibly empty prefix leading from the requested root. -/
inductive Reaches (g : Graph R) : R → R → Prop where
  | here (r) : Reaches g r r
  | step : (g r).next = some s → Reaches g s t → Reaches g r t

/-- Both branches return a concrete endpoint. The cycle is nonempty and is
reachable from the requested start, even when there is an initial tail. -/
inductive WalkResult (g : FiniteGraph n) (r : Fin n) (fuel : Nat) : Type where
  | terminal (distance : Nat) (vertex : Fin n) :
      distance < fuel → Ends g r distance → (g vertex).next = none →
      Observes g r (g vertex) → WalkResult g r fuel
  | cycle (vertex : Fin n) : TransparentPath g vertex vertex →
      Reaches g r vertex → WalkResult g r fuel

/-- Every saved vertex has a nonempty path to the current vertex. Repetition
therefore constructs a cycle, including after a nonempty tail. -/
def walkAux (g : FiniteGraph n) (fuel : Nat) :
    (seen : List (Fin n)) → (r : Fin n) →
    seen.Nodup → seen.length + fuel = n →
    (∀ s, s ∈ seen → TransparentPath g s r) → WalkResult g r fuel :=
  match fuel with
  | 0 => fun seen r hd hsize hp =>
      if hm : r ∈ seen then .cycle r (hp r hm) (.here r)
      else False.elim (by
        have hb := finite_list_bound (List.nodup_cons.mpr ⟨hm, hd⟩)
        simp only [List.length_cons] at hb
        omega)
  | fuel + 1 => fun seen r hd hsize hp =>
      if hm : r ∈ seen then .cycle r (hp r hm) (.here r)
      else match hn : (g r).next with
      | none => .terminal 0 r (Nat.zero_lt_succ _) (.done r hn) hn (.done r hn)
      | some s =>
          let hd' : (r :: seen).Nodup := List.nodup_cons.mpr ⟨hm, hd⟩
          let hp' : ∀ t, t ∈ r :: seen → TransparentPath g t s := by
            intro t ht
            rcases List.mem_cons.mp ht with he | ht
            · subst t; exact .edge hn
            · exact path_trans (hp t ht) (.edge hn)
          match walkAux g fuel (r :: seen) s hd' (by simp only [List.length_cons]; omega) hp' with
          | .terminal k vertex hk he ht ho =>
              .terminal (k + 1) vertex (by omega) (.step hn he) ht (.step hn ho)
          | .cycle c hc reachable => .cycle c hc (.step hn reachable)

def walk (g : FiniteGraph n) (r : Fin n) : WalkResult g r n :=
  walkAux g n [] r (by simp) (by simp) (by intro s hs; cases hs)

def NoCycle (g : Graph R) : Prop := ∀ r, ¬ TransparentPath g r r

def AllEnd (g : FiniteGraph n) : Prop := ∀ r, ∃ k, k < n ∧ Ends g r k

theorem allEnd_of_noCycle {g : FiniteGraph n} (hc : NoCycle g) : AllEnd g := by
  intro r
  cases walk g r with
  | terminal k _ hk he _ _ => exact ⟨k, hk, he⟩
  | cycle c hp _ => exact False.elim (hc c hp)

/-- Rank is computed uniformly by n steps of the actual successor function.
The proof input provides no numeric ranks and is not used computationally. -/
def guardOfAllEnd (g : FiniteGraph n) (he : AllEnd g) : Guarded g where
  rank := height g n
  ceiling := n
  bound := by
    intro r
    obtain ⟨k, hk, hr⟩ := he r
    rw [ends_height hr n (by omega)]
    exact hk
  decrease := by
    intro r s hs
    obtain ⟨k, hk, hr⟩ := he r
    have er := ends_height hr n (by omega)
    cases hr with
    | done r hn => rw [hn] at hs; cases hs
    | @step r t k ht htail =>
        have ets : t = s := Option.some.inj (ht.symm.trans hs)
        subst t
        have es := ends_height htail n (by omega)
        change height g n s < height g n r
        rw [er, es]
        omega

def guardOfNoCycle (g : FiniteGraph n) (hc : NoCycle g) : Guarded g :=
  guardOfAllEnd g (allEnd_of_noCycle hc)

theorem guarded_iff_noCycle (g : FiniteGraph n) :
    Nonempty (Guarded g) ↔ NoCycle g := by
  constructor
  · intro ⟨guard⟩ r hp
    exact no_transparent_cycle guard r hp
  · intro hc
    exact ⟨guardOfNoCycle g hc⟩

/-- Canonical observation now needs only the finite cycle criterion. -/
theorem finite_reference_canonical {g : FiniteGraph n} {xi : Fin n → Ty}
    (hg : WellTyped g xi) (hc : NoCycle g) (r : Fin n) :
    ∃ node, Observes g r node ∧ Canonical (xi r) node :=
  reference_canonical hg (guardOfNoCycle g hc) r

theorem finite_no_bottom {g : FiniteGraph n} {xi : Fin n → Ty}
    (hg : WellTyped g xi) (hc : NoCycle g) (r : Fin n) : xi r ≠ .bottom :=
  no_bottom_reference hg (guardOfNoCycle g hc) r

inductive ScanResult (g : FiniteGraph n) (xs : List (Fin n)) : Type where
  | terminals : (∀ r, r ∈ xs → ∃ k, k < n ∧ Ends g r k) → ScanResult g xs
  | cycle (vertex : Fin n) : TransparentPath g vertex vertex → ScanResult g xs

def scan (g : FiniteGraph n) : (xs : List (Fin n)) → ScanResult g xs
  | [] => .terminals (by intro r hr; cases hr)
  | r :: xs => match walk g r with
    | .cycle c hc _ => .cycle c hc
    | .terminal k _ hk he _ _ => match scan g xs with
      | .cycle c hc => .cycle c hc
      | .terminals hs => .terminals (by
          intro s hmem
          rcases List.mem_cons.mp hmem with heq | hmem
          · subst s; exact ⟨k, hk, he⟩
          · exact hs s hmem)

inductive GuardDecision (g : FiniteGraph n) : Type where
  | guarded : Guarded g → GuardDecision g
  | cycle (vertex : Fin n) : TransparentPath g vertex vertex → GuardDecision g

/-- Total finite algorithm, with either a computed certificate or explicit cycle.
The empty graph requires no start vertex and returns a certificate. -/
def decideGuard (g : FiniteGraph n) : GuardDecision g :=
  match scan g (List.finRange n) with
  | .cycle c hc => .cycle c hc
  | .terminals hs => .guarded (guardOfAllEnd g (fun r => hs r (List.mem_finRange r)))

def noCycleDecidable (g : FiniteGraph n) : Decidable (NoCycle g) :=
  match decideGuard g with
  | .guarded guard => isTrue (fun r hp => no_transparent_cycle guard r hp)
  | .cycle c hc => isFalse (fun h => h c hc)

/-- Project only new-to-new transparent edges. An old target is terminal for
this local check, since allocate never introduces old-to-new edges. -/
def freshGraph (fresh : Fin n → Node (Sum R (Fin n))) : FiniteGraph n := fun s =>
  match (fresh s).next with
  | some (.inr t) => .alias t
  | _ => .unit

theorem freshGraph_edge (fresh : Fin n → Node (Sum R (Fin n))) (s t : Fin n) :
    (freshGraph fresh s).next = some t ↔ (fresh s).next = some (.inr t) := by
  unfold freshGraph
  cases hn : (fresh s).next with
  | none => simp [Node.next]
  | some target => cases target <;> simp [Node.next]

/-- Local criterion: exactly fresh-internal transparent cycles are forbidden. -/
def FreshNoCycle (fresh : Fin n → Node (Sum R (Fin n))) : Prop :=
  NoCycle (freshGraph fresh)

def allocateFiniteGuard {g : Graph R} (guard : Guarded g)
    (fresh : Fin n → Node (Sum R (Fin n))) (hc : FreshNoCycle fresh) :
    Guarded (allocate g fresh) :=
  let localGuard := guardOfNoCycle (freshGraph fresh) hc
  allocate_guard guard fresh localGuard.rank localGuard.ceiling localGuard.bound
    (fun s t he => localGuard.decrease s t ((freshGraph_edge fresh s t).mpr he))

/-- The original rec extension conclusion, with supplied local ranks, ceiling,
bounds and decreases removed. The original node/body typing premises remain. -/
theorem finite_rec_extension {g : Graph R} {xi : R → Ty} {nu : Fin n → Ty}
    (hg : WellTyped g xi) (guard : Guarded g)
    (fresh : Fin n → Node (Sum R (Fin n)))
    (hf : ∀ s, NodeTyped (joinTy xi nu) (fresh s) (nu s))
    (hc : FreshNoCycle fresh)
    {body : Term R (Fin n)} {a : Ty} (hb : Typed xi nu body a) :
    WellTyped (allocate g fresh) (joinTy xi nu) ∧
    (∀ r, ∃ node, Observes (allocate g fresh) r node ∧ Canonical (joinTy xi nu r) node) ∧
    Typed (joinTy xi nu) emptyTy (closeBody body) a := by
  have ht := allocate_typed hg fresh hf
  exact ⟨ht, reference_canonical ht (allocateFiniteGuard guard fresh hc), closeBody_typed hb⟩

/-- If the entire old graph is finite, its supplied rank disappears as well. -/
theorem finite_rec_extension_from_cycles {g : FiniteGraph m} {xi : Fin m → Ty}
    {nu : Fin n → Ty} (hg : WellTyped g xi) (hcOld : NoCycle g)
    (fresh : Fin n → Node (Sum (Fin m) (Fin n)))
    (hf : ∀ s, NodeTyped (joinTy xi nu) (fresh s) (nu s))
    (hcFresh : FreshNoCycle fresh)
    {body : Term (Fin m) (Fin n)} {a : Ty} (hb : Typed xi nu body a) :
    WellTyped (allocate g fresh) (joinTy xi nu) ∧
    (∀ r, ∃ node, Observes (allocate g fresh) r node ∧ Canonical (joinTy xi nu r) node) ∧
    Typed (joinTy xi nu) emptyTy (closeBody body) a :=
  finite_rec_extension hg (guardOfNoCycle g hcOld) fresh hf hcFresh hb

/-- The projection is an exact supplier of real allocated transparent paths. -/
theorem fresh_path_allocation {g : Graph R}
    {fresh : Fin n → Node (Sum R (Fin n))} {s t : Fin n}
    (h : TransparentPath (freshGraph fresh) s t) :
    TransparentPath (allocate g fresh) (.inr s) (.inr t) := by
  induction h with
  | edge he =>
      apply TransparentPath.edge
      exact (freshGraph_edge fresh _ _).mp he
  | cons he _ ih =>
      apply TransparentPath.cons _ ih
      exact (freshGraph_edge fresh _ _).mp he

/-- Given the original old certificate, the finite local cycle test is also
necessary, so it is not a stronger sufficient condition introduced for proofs. -/
theorem allocate_guard_iff {g : Graph R} (guard : Guarded g)
    (fresh : Fin n → Node (Sum R (Fin n))) :
    Nonempty (Guarded (allocate g fresh)) ↔ FreshNoCycle fresh := by
  constructor
  · intro ⟨post⟩ s hs
    exact no_transparent_cycle post (.inr s) (fresh_path_allocation hs)
  · intro hc
    exact ⟨allocateFiniteGuard guard fresh hc⟩

theorem noCycle_of_terminal {g : FiniteGraph n}
    (ht : ∀ r, (g r).next = none) : NoCycle g := by
  have he : AllEnd g := by
    intro r
    exact ⟨0, by have := r.isLt; omega, .done r (ht r)⟩
  intro r hp
  exact no_transparent_cycle (guardOfAllEnd g he) r hp

/-- Arbitrarily long chains, including the maximal n-edge chain on n+1 nodes.
This supplies the exact distance, not an assumed rank or termination fact. -/
def countdown (n : Nat) : FiniteGraph (n + 1) := fun r =>
  match hv : r.val with
  | 0 => .unit
  | k + 1 => .alias ⟨k, by have := r.isLt; omega⟩

theorem countdown_ends (n : Nat) (r : Fin (n + 1)) :
    Ends (countdown n) r r.val := by
  have aux : ∀ k (hk : k < n + 1), Ends (countdown n) ⟨k, hk⟩ k := by
    intro k
    induction k with
    | zero => intro hk; exact .done _ rfl
    | succ k ih =>
        intro hk
        exact .step rfl (ih (by omega))
  exact aux r.val r.isLt

theorem countdown_noCycle (n : Nat) : NoCycle (countdown n) := by
  intro r hp
  have he : AllEnd (countdown n) := fun s => ⟨s.val, s.isLt, countdown_ends n s⟩
  exact no_transparent_cycle (guardOfAllEnd _ he) r hp

theorem countdown_exact_height (n : Nat) (r : Fin (n + 1)) :
    height (countdown n) (n + 1) r = r.val :=
  ends_height (countdown_ends n r) (n + 1) (Nat.le_of_lt r.isLt)

def selfCycle : FiniteGraph 1 := fun r => .alias r

theorem selfCycle_rejected : ¬ NoCycle selfCycle := by
  intro hc
  exact hc 0 (.edge rfl)

def cycleWithTail : FiniteGraph 3 := fun r =>
  if r.val = 0 then .alias 1 else .alias 2

theorem tail_reaches_cycle : TransparentPath cycleWithTail 0 2 :=
  .cons rfl (.edge rfl)

theorem tail_cycle_explicit : TransparentPath cycleWithTail 2 2 := .edge rfl

theorem tail_cycle_rejected : ¬ NoCycle cycleWithTail :=
  fun hc => hc 2 tail_cycle_explicit

/-- Whole-graph cycles through data fields remain admissible to the guard test.
No recursive type equation or typing claim is fabricated for this pair. -/
def dataSelfCycle : FiniteGraph 1 := fun r => .pair r r

theorem dataSelfCycle_allowed : NoCycle dataSelfCycle :=
  noCycle_of_terminal (fun _ => rfl)

def sharedTerminal : FiniteGraph 3 := fun r =>
  if r.val = 0 then .unit else .alias 0

theorem sharedTerminal_ends (r : Fin 3) :
    ∃ k, k < 3 ∧ Ends sharedTerminal r k := by
  by_cases h : r.val = 0
  · exact ⟨0, by omega, .done r (by simp [sharedTerminal, h, Node.next])⟩
  · exact ⟨1, by omega, .step (by simp [sharedTerminal, h, Node.next]) (.done 0 rfl)⟩

def sharedTerminal_guard : Guarded sharedTerminal :=
  guardOfAllEnd sharedTerminal sharedTerminal_ends

/-- Both actual lambda bodies call the opposite fresh graph reference. -/
def finiteMutualLambda : FiniteGraph 2 := fun r =>
  .lam .unit .unit (.app (.ref (if r.val = 0 then 1 else 0)) (.var none))

theorem finiteMutualLambda_typed :
    WellTyped finiteMutualLambda (fun _ => .arrow .unit .unit) := by
  intro r
  exact NodeTyped.lam (Typed.app (Typed.ref _) (Typed.var none))

theorem finiteMutualLambda_noCycle : NoCycle finiteMutualLambda :=
  noCycle_of_terminal (fun _ => rfl)

def finiteMutualLambda_guard : Guarded finiteMutualLambda :=
  guardOfNoCycle finiteMutualLambda finiteMutualLambda_noCycle

/-- Fresh-to-old transparent references are accepted without a local rank input,
even when the old reference sort is infinite. -/
def oldAliasFresh (old : R) : Fin 1 → Node (Sum R (Fin 1)) :=
  fun _ => .alias (.inl old)

theorem oldAliasFresh_noCycle (old : R) : FreshNoCycle (oldAliasFresh old) :=
  noCycle_of_terminal (fun _ => rfl)

def oldAliasAllocation_guard {g : Graph R} (guard : Guarded g) (old : R) :
    Guarded (allocate g (oldAliasFresh old)) :=
  allocateFiniteGuard guard (oldAliasFresh old) (oldAliasFresh_noCycle old)

/-- A graph with zero nodes has a computed certificate without a root oracle. -/
def zeroGraph : FiniteGraph 0 := fun r => Fin.elim0 r

def zeroGraph_guard : Guarded zeroGraph :=
  guardOfNoCycle zeroGraph (fun r => Fin.elim0 r)

end YulangClosure.GuardedValueGraph.FiniteDecision

# Finite transparent guard completeness — candidate revision 1

Parent: GVG-GUARD-COMPLETE-1, under GUARD-INTERACTION-THEORY-20261025/r1.
Status: constructive Lean candidate, NOT_CHECKED and NOT_REVIEWED by this author.
Author: /root/finite_guard_completeness_astra_r1; requested gpt-6-astra/medium;
observed model/effort UNKNOWN. No coauthors or descendants at author freeze.
No production authority or native correspondence is claimed.

## Original claim and actual construction

For every n and every existing GuardedValueGraph.FiniteGraph n, the sole traversed
edge is the existing Node.next. No additional property of the graph or node
bodies is assumed by walk or decideGuard. The constructor domain is exactly the
accepted unit/pair/lam/delay/alias/view/roll/evidence research domain. In particular,
roll/view/evidence remain identity-typed in this model; this does not prove the
paper's type-changing forms.

walkAux structurally recurses on fuel. It carries a duplicate-free list seen,
seen.length + fuel = n, and a nonempty transparent path from each saved vertex
to the current vertex. Membership immediately supplies an actual cycle. For a
new vertex, Node.next = none returns that vertex, a terminality proof, exact
distance and Observes proof. A successor consumes one fuel unit and extends all
saved paths by the actual edge. At zero fuel a new vertex would give a
nodup list of n+1 members of Fin n, contradicting the constructive finite-list
bound. Thus this branch is impossible for the supplied invariants; it is not an
assumed traversal-termination fact. The cycle branch also carries Reaches from
the requested root, so a tail entering a cycle is covered.

The terminal distance is strictly less than n. height g n r computes a natural
number solely by n iterations of actual Node.next. ends_height identifies it
with the exact terminal distance once enough fuel is available. The endpoint
and distance supplied by walk derive AllEnd from NoCycle, then guardOfAllEnd
constructs rank = height g n, ceiling = n, the strict bound and strict descent
on every actual transparent edge. Its AllEnd premise is discharged by
allEnd_of_noCycle; no rank existence, chosen minimum, choice, well-foundedness
oracle or assumed termination enters the main result.

guarded_iff_noCycle combines guardOfNoCycle with the accepted
no_transparent_cycle converse. scan runs walk on the explicit List.finRange n;
decideGuard returns a computed Guarded certificate or a concrete vertex and
nonempty TransparentPath cycle. noCycleDecidable packages the same executable
case split. The empty graph needs no arbitrary starting vertex. Each root walk
uses at most n successor inspections and n+1 membership checks; scan repeats
this finite computation over n roots. This is a simple research decision,
without a native efficiency claim or benchmark.

## Application to original graph and rec extension

finite_reference_canonical and finite_no_bottom apply the constructed certificate
to the accepted canonical-observation and bottom-exclusion lemmas immediately.
Their only graph hypotheses are the original WellTyped assignment and NoCycle.

freshGraph keeps exactly those fresh Node.next edges whose target is Sum.inr;
none and old targets are terminal only for this local analysis. freshGraph_edge
proves the exact equivalence to the original fresh node's successor equation.
fresh_path_allocation transports the resulting nonempty paths to actual
allocate nodes. This makes the local criterion auditable against its constructor,
not an independently assumed transition system.

allocateFiniteGuard derives local rank, ceiling, bound and decrease from
FreshNoCycle and feeds them to the accepted allocate_guard. It allows all
fresh-to-old edges and retains the original old certificate. allocate_guard_iff
also proves necessity of the local cycle criterion under that old certificate.
finite_rec_extension supplies the original conjunction: post-allocation graph
typing, typed canonical observation of every old/new reference, and the typed
simultaneously closed body. The original old typing, per-fresh-node typing and
body typing premises remain intact. finite_rec_extension_from_cycles removes
the old supplied certificate too when the old graph is finite.

This is an application to the parent mathematical obstruction, not another
assumed-rank theorem. Subject to successful elaboration and fresh independent
review, it supplies the exact missing finite-rank completeness direction.
Luna alone adjudicates that local gate. Full-paper and native parent gates remain
OPEN regardless of the local result.

## Falsifiers and boundaries

The Lean candidate includes the following concrete constructions and quantified
proofs, not executed tests:

- zeroGraph and zeroGraph_guard handle n=0; decideGuard itself scans an empty list.
- countdown n has n+1 vertices and a maximal n-edge transparent chain.
  countdown_ends and countdown_exact_height establish its exact distance for
  every vertex; no off-by-one escape is assumed.
- selfCycle_rejected excludes a transparent self-alias.
- cycleWithTail has 0→1→2→2; tail_reaches_cycle, tail_cycle_explicit and
  tail_cycle_rejected expose both the tail and the nonempty cycle.
- sharedTerminal has two aliases reaching the same terminal; its certificate is
  obtained from constructed endpoint proofs.
- finiteMutualLambda contains two actual lambda bodies calling the opposite
  reference; its node typing and NoCycle are constructed. This permits recursive
  computation and makes no claim that evaluation terminates.
- dataSelfCycle passes the outer guard test because pair fields are genuine
  guards. No impossible finite recursive Ty equation or node-typing derivation
  is claimed for that self-pair.
- oldAliasFresh and oldAliasAllocation_guard allow a new alias to any old node,
  including an old reference domain that is not finite.

The universal proofs cover every mixed alias/view/roll/evidence chain and cycle,
all concrete data/code nodes, sharing, graph size zero and arbitrary finite size.
No whole-graph DAG condition is introduced. The list bound is reproved with
explicit DecidableEq because the general library Nodup.length_le_of_subset
proof uses classical equality. Library source for the used Fin/list/erase
lemmas was inspected; the primary must still inspect the full emitted axiom
closure. No sorry, new axiom, Classical.choice or native_decide is used in the
candidate source.

## Reuse and remaining owners

Reused only within accepted premises: GuardedValueGraph.no_transparent_cycle,
reference_canonical, no_bottom_reference, allocate_guard, allocate_typed and
closeBody_typed. The old rank-based rec_extension remains immutable; the new
finite theorem supplies its missing rank inputs instead of changing semantics.
The paper's graph-extension/value-form passages motivate the parent but do not
supply machine-checked full-paper RHS or type-changing-form premises. No prior
failed construction is revived, and no historical result is generalized by
analogy. No actual compiler/native source audit is claimed.

FGD-CHECK-1 — Luna owns primary elaboration, dependency/axiom inspection, repairs
only after acknowledged author STOP and fresh nonauthor review. Falsifier: any
elaboration failure, forbidden axiom, or finite graph for which the produced
terminal/cycle witness or strict rank equation is invalid. The exact source
suppliers are walkAux/height/freshGraph; consumers are guardOfNoCycle,
allocateFiniteGuard and finite_rec_extension. No production edit is needed.

GVG-FORMS-1 — full-paper graph proof owner: actual mu, type-changing roll/views,
type evidence and missing eliminators. Falsifier: transparent traversal preserves
this model's type but fails the real eliminator's required evidence.
GVG-REC-RHS-1 — full-paper syntax/binder owner: derive fresh NodeTyped premises
from full original rec RHS derivations under all actual binders. Existing Term
substitution covers its own five-constructor domain only.
ENV-GRAPH-1 — Luna/source intake: native graph realization from current cells,
initialization/preallocation and machine.rs Instruction::Lambda,
Frame::ValueEntry, Machine::lookup/extend and Callee, plus receiving.rs lambda
schema construction. Current graph mathematics does not establish those source
constructors emit this representation or satisfy its typing/cycle conditions.
Original F1/FK1, foreign continuations, Simple-sub generation/accumulation/
propagation/levels/extrusion/qualifying intrusion/generalization remain untouched.

# Higher-order research core and structural embedding

Status: Draft research construction; checking and review evidence is recorded in
the sprint outcome and its frozen receipts. This is not production authority.
Scope: frozen LEAN-HIGHER-ORDER-PROOF-CORE-20261025/r1 research representation.
Initial author: /root/higher_order_proof_core_astra_r1; requested gpt-6-astra/medium,
observed model/effort UNKNOWN. Primary /root repairs and integrates after author
STOP; the outcome records final authorship and independent review. No descendants.
Production authority: none. The operational paper is a proposal/target; the
2026-10-07 complete-Call definition §1 records permission for legitimate research
definitions, not adoption of this representation as compiler architecture.

The parent RESPONSE-ENCODING-1 / ENV-CALLABLE-1 lacked a callable constructor in
its formal Value sort. The candidate removes that specific representational
obstruction by constructing a new callable type and actual lambda/wrap values.
Every Original.Val/Comp and TypedCall.Value/Comp/Adapter/Function constructor is
mapped structurally. No old term is retained behind an opaque original opcode.
The full parent, native readback and operational safety remain OPEN.

## Syntax and quantifiers

`HigherOrderSyntax.lean` retains every old type constructor, all eight literal
domains and their exact payload representations, variables, delay, injections,
single-child intersection/top values and all seven Original computations. It
adds the existing Call view/scope/expose/request/fail nodes, lambda/wrap values,
and dynamicCall. Request's continuation binds its operation instance's response
type. The type language can place callable types beneath thunk/union/intersection
and in operation instances. The value, computation and adapter syntax is mutually
inductive; all typing judgments are defined afterwards.

Value-entry lambda binds A; computation-entry lambda binds Thunk A. Both retain
receipt, annotated input/body/result types, body and result consumer. Wrap keeps
the input adapter c→a and output adapter b→d around an a→b function. DynamicCall
accepts a thunk carrier. This fixes a research typing interface without asserting
an execution rule or operational equivalence for the new constructor.

`ContextEmbedding old new` quantifies over every old lookup fact. The mutual
Original and TypedCall preservation proofs quantify over arbitrary old terms,
old typing derivations and target contexts satisfying that relation. Closed
Original nodes embed under any target context using the empty lookup relation;
binders use `extend_embedding`. The Function theorem quantifies over every old
FunctionTyped derivation and every target context. No original constructor,
source-domain restriction or independent continuation quantifier is discarded.
This is one-way typing preservation, not reflection or full conservativity.

## Metadata boundary

Paths retain component lists, port kinds and translated endpoint types;
occurrences retain identities and paths. Operation instances retain operation
identity, ordered type arguments and both payload/response types. Receipt slots
and profiles retain order, identity and typed paths. Adapter metadata retains
all path correspondences and captured occurrences. Interface-port metadata also
has a structural map.

PathRule is a Prop in the accepted input. `embedPathRule` translates its proof
into a new Prop proof. It does not eliminate that proof into a data-valued map
identity. In particular the old permissive adapterMap rule remains permissive;
this work cannot prove that a mappingIdentity absent from runtime data can be
reconstructed. Syntax is **typing-proof-free**, not entirely proof-free. The old
Adapter.typed field is omitted from syntax and consumed solely to construct the
new extrinsic AdapterTyped derivation. The retained PathRule metadata neither
contains a typing judgment nor creates a typing-definition cycle.

## Parent application

`embedFunction_typed` constructs a ValueTyped callable from an old FunctionTyped
proof. `function_as_argument` and `call_with_function_argument` use it in the
actual new delayed argument and dynamicCall constructors.
`request_callable_response` constructs a request that binds and returns a
callable-typed response. `function_cell` pushes the embedded function into the
existing generic NativeClosureEnvironment.Store, proves the actual current cell
equality and supplies its callable typing derivation.

`read_embedding` preserves the exact old selected cell address while mapping the
current store pointwise. `read_embedding_typed` combines that equation with the
accepted `successful_read_typed` theorem. `captured_value_typed` applies the
accepted `realized_substitution_typed` supplier to each represented context index;
`captured_body_typed` applies its actual successful capture and closed-body
construction before embedding. Both keep successful realization and CellsTyped
as explicit original premises. Nothing claims that arbitrary native closures
already satisfy those premises, or that old stores already represent new
callable values. Generic new callable storage and old represented-read transport
are two separate constructions whose native connection is still open.

## Remaining source obligations and reuse

Accepted CoreSyntax typing and CallEnvironmentRealization supply precisely their
existing domains. CoreSubstitution's bind/request lifting is reused through
close_body, without reproving lookup or assuming a new substitution rule. The
NativeClosureEnvironment.Store remains generic; no machine fields change.
Historical literal readback is not extended to callable readback by analogy.
No failure is dismissed by a narrower theorem; no new source restriction,
Simple-sub bypass or production implementation is introduced.

Luna/source intake owns ENV-LAYOUT-1 (resolved free-variable order and binder
indices from source Lambda/Name/Apply), ENV-CELL-VALUE-1 (current native Value
encoding), ENV-GRAPH-1 (recursive cell/closure graphs), ENV-CALLABLE-1's remaining
native body/consumer mapping, and ENV-DISPATCH-1. Relevant native owners remain
machine.rs `Instruction::Lambda`, `Frame::ValueEntry`, `Machine::lookup`,
`Machine::extend`, closure/Callee branches and receiving.rs lambda schema
construction. The primary's disjoint source map gives their complete exact
producer/consumer inventory, including unit/record/default entry cases.
Force, native transitions, new-core substitution/progress/preservation,
whole-trace safety, operation authenticity and original inference A/B remain
OPEN. No F1/FK1 or foreign-continuation theorem is claimed here.

## Intake and checks

No Lean/build/tests/native checks were run by the author. A shell `python`
invocation failed because the executable was absent; the generation was then
performed with python3. This was a file-writing failure before any write, not a
failed proof check. Primary owns bounded elaboration, public signature/axiom
inspection, distinguishing examples, repairs after author STOP and fresh
independent review. Author/coauthor cannot independently certify this candidate.
Only the four exact leased files were created; there are no scratch paths,
background processes, descendants, compiler changes or Git operations.

# Finite transparent guard completeness — candidate revision 1

Parent: GVG-GUARD-COMPLETE-1, under GUARD-INTERACTION-THEORY-20261025/r1.
Status: constructive Lean candidate, NOT_CHECKED and NOT_REVIEWED by this author.
Author: /root/finite_guard_completeness_astra_r1; requested gpt-6-astra/medium;
observed model/effort UNKNOWN. No coauthors or descendants at author freeze.
No production authority or native correspondence is claimed.

## Original claim and actual construction

For every n and every existing GuardedValueGraph.FiniteGraph n, the sole traversed
edge is the existing Node.next. No additional property of the graph or node
bodies is assumed by walk or decideGuard. The constructor domain is exactly the
accepted unit/pair/lam/delay/alias/view/roll/evidence research domain. In particular,
roll/view/evidence remain identity-typed in this model; this does not prove the
paper's type-changing forms.

walkAux structurally recurses on fuel. It carries a duplicate-free list seen,
seen.length + fuel = n, and a nonempty transparent path from each saved vertex
to the current vertex. Membership immediately supplies an actual cycle. For a
new vertex, Node.next = none returns that vertex, a terminality proof, exact
distance and Observes proof. A successor consumes one fuel unit and extends all
saved paths by the actual edge. At zero fuel a new vertex would give a
nodup list of n+1 members of Fin n, contradicting the constructive finite-list
bound. Thus this branch is impossible for the supplied invariants; it is not an
assumed traversal-termination fact. The cycle branch also carries Reaches from
the requested root, so a tail entering a cycle is covered.

The terminal distance is strictly less than n. height g n r computes a natural
number solely by n iterations of actual Node.next. ends_height identifies it
with the exact terminal distance once enough fuel is available. The endpoint
and distance supplied by walk derive AllEnd from NoCycle, then guardOfAllEnd
constructs rank = height g n, ceiling = n, the strict bound and strict descent
on every actual transparent edge. Its AllEnd premise is discharged by
allEnd_of_noCycle; no rank existence, chosen minimum, choice, well-foundedness
oracle or assumed termination enters the main result.

guarded_iff_noCycle combines guardOfNoCycle with the accepted
no_transparent_cycle converse. scan runs walk on the explicit List.finRange n;
decideGuard returns a computed Guarded certificate or a concrete vertex and
nonempty TransparentPath cycle. noCycleDecidable packages the same executable
case split. The empty graph needs no arbitrary starting vertex. Each root walk
uses at most n successor inspections and n+1 membership checks; scan repeats
this finite computation over n roots. This is a simple research decision,
without a native efficiency claim or benchmark.

## Application to original graph and rec extension

finite_reference_canonical and finite_no_bottom apply the constructed certificate
to the accepted canonical-observation and bottom-exclusion lemmas immediately.
Their only graph hypotheses are the original WellTyped assignment and NoCycle.

freshGraph keeps exactly those fresh Node.next edges whose target is Sum.inr;
none and old targets are terminal only for this local analysis. freshGraph_edge
proves the exact equivalence to the original fresh node's successor equation.
fresh_path_allocation transports the resulting nonempty paths to actual
allocate nodes. This makes the local criterion auditable against its constructor,
not an independently assumed transition system.

allocateFiniteGuard derives local rank, ceiling, bound and decrease from
FreshNoCycle and feeds them to the accepted allocate_guard. It allows all
fresh-to-old edges and retains the original old certificate. allocate_guard_iff
also proves necessity of the local cycle criterion under that old certificate.
finite_rec_extension supplies the original conjunction: post-allocation graph
typing, typed canonical observation of every old/new reference, and the typed
simultaneously closed body. The original old typing, per-fresh-node typing and
body typing premises remain intact. finite_rec_extension_from_cycles removes
the old supplied certificate too when the old graph is finite.

This is an application to the parent mathematical obstruction, not another
assumed-rank theorem. Subject to successful elaboration and fresh independent
review, it supplies the exact missing finite-rank completeness direction.
Luna alone adjudicates that local gate. Full-paper and native parent gates remain
OPEN regardless of the local result.

## Falsifiers and boundaries

The Lean candidate includes the following concrete constructions and quantified
proofs, not executed tests:

- zeroGraph and zeroGraph_guard handle n=0; decideGuard itself scans an empty list.
- countdown n has n+1 vertices and a maximal n-edge transparent chain.
  countdown_ends and countdown_exact_height establish its exact distance for
  every vertex; no off-by-one escape is assumed.
- selfCycle_rejected excludes a transparent self-alias.
- cycleWithTail has 0→1→2→2; tail_reaches_cycle, tail_cycle_explicit and
  tail_cycle_rejected expose both the tail and the nonempty cycle.
- sharedTerminal has two aliases reaching the same terminal; its certificate is
  obtained from constructed endpoint proofs.
- finiteMutualLambda contains two actual lambda bodies calling the opposite
  reference; its node typing and NoCycle are constructed. This permits recursive
  computation and makes no claim that evaluation terminates.
- dataSelfCycle passes the outer guard test because pair fields are genuine
  guards. No impossible finite recursive Ty equation or node-typing derivation
  is claimed for that self-pair.
- oldAliasFresh and oldAliasAllocation_guard allow a new alias to any old node,
  including an old reference domain that is not finite.

The universal proofs cover every mixed alias/view/roll/evidence chain and cycle,
all concrete data/code nodes, sharing, graph size zero and arbitrary finite size.
No whole-graph DAG condition is introduced. The list bound is reproved with
explicit DecidableEq because the general library Nodup.length_le_of_subset
proof uses classical equality. Library source for the used Fin/list/erase
lemmas was inspected; the primary must still inspect the full emitted axiom
closure. No sorry, new axiom, Classical.choice or native_decide is used in the
candidate source.

## Reuse and remaining owners

Reused only within accepted premises: GuardedValueGraph.no_transparent_cycle,
reference_canonical, no_bottom_reference, allocate_guard, allocate_typed and
closeBody_typed. The old rank-based rec_extension remains immutable; the new
finite theorem supplies its missing rank inputs instead of changing semantics.
The paper's graph-extension/value-form passages motivate the parent but do not
supply machine-checked full-paper RHS or type-changing-form premises. No prior
failed construction is revived, and no historical result is generalized by
analogy. No actual compiler/native source audit is claimed.

FGD-CHECK-1 — Luna owns primary elaboration, dependency/axiom inspection, repairs
only after acknowledged author STOP and fresh nonauthor review. Falsifier: any
elaboration failure, forbidden axiom, or finite graph for which the produced
terminal/cycle witness or strict rank equation is invalid. The exact source
suppliers are walkAux/height/freshGraph; consumers are guardOfNoCycle,
allocateFiniteGuard and finite_rec_extension. No production edit is needed.

GVG-FORMS-1 — full-paper graph proof owner: actual mu, type-changing roll/views,
type evidence and missing eliminators. Falsifier: transparent traversal preserves
this model's type but fails the real eliminator's required evidence.
GVG-REC-RHS-1 — full-paper syntax/binder owner: derive fresh NodeTyped premises
from full original rec RHS derivations under all actual binders. Existing Term
substitution covers its own five-constructor domain only.
ENV-GRAPH-1 — Luna/source intake: native graph realization from current cells,
initialization/preallocation and machine.rs Instruction::Lambda,
Frame::ValueEntry, Machine::lookup/extend and Callee, plus receiving.rs lambda
schema construction. Current graph mathematics does not establish those source
constructors emit this representation or satisfy its typing/cycle conditions.
Original F1/FK1, foreign continuations, Simple-sub generation/accumulation/

# Higher-order repeated interaction value safety

Status: candidate mathematics; author has NOT_RUN Lean, tests or builds. Fresh
independent review and primary elaboration are pending. No production authority.
Author: `/root/higher_order_interaction_astra_r1`, requested `gpt-6-astra/medium`,
observed model/effort UNKNOWN. No descendants or other contributing authors at
this author freeze. Any primary repair after acknowledged STOP adds coauthorship.
Contract: `GUARD-INTERACTION-THEORY-20261025/r1`, lane B, HO-INTERACTION-1.
Baseline: `e9c0a89d2f92ac0116a75e5c7e24623e4c38acd9` (supplied; no Git invoked).

## Original parent and exact contribution

The original parent is the execution type-safety theorem in
`docs/yulang-operational-type-safety-ja.tex:1139`–1159. It quantifies over every
finite prefix of internal transitions, typed external responses and multiple
resumptions, allowing stopping at a request; returned callback code is typed.
Its graph extension and metadata clauses remain part of that original claim.
The request-cut lemma at 1047–1066 and raw resume discussion at 458–472 are the
precise supporting parent obligations. They are research targets, not adopted
compiler semantics.

The new module `lean/YulangClosure/HigherOrderInteraction.lean` supplies a
candidate repeated-interaction proof for the accepted finite HigherOrder
research grammar. The response, saved handle, outer evaluation context and
finite trace are independently quantified. It extends the accepted internal
trace safety construction with real request capture and arbitrary old-handle
responses. It does not substitute one lambda frame action for F1/FK1 or identify
this value-typing projection with the paper's complete raw Resume operation.

`closed_program_interaction_safety` starts with only a closed typed computation
and an EMPTY saved arena. `finite_saved_response_safety` applies the result to
ANY entry captured during ANY such finite trace and ANY closed response having
that entry's own operation response type. It supplies actual publication
provenance, the original result type, all saved-entry typing, and resumed
progress. Thus captured continuation typing is not an assumed initial resource.

## Raw construction and proof chain

`Saved` retains the full operation instance, exact payload, original
response-binding continuation and entire `Safety.EvalContext`. Its fields carry
no typing derivations. An arena is a finite list. Handles are natural-number
positions; publication appends at the old length. `lookup_append_old`,
`lookup_append_fresh` and `lookup_length_none` establish stable old entries and a
fresh position. No allocation or response mutates any old saved record.

`RawStep.internal` embeds the accepted `Safety.Step`; `RawStep.publish` matches
only a current computation that IS the saved context plugged with that exact
request; `RawStep.response` looks up an existing handle and substitutes the
provided raw value into its original response binder before plugging the entire
saved context. Response is permitted from any phase and any old handle, so an
external scheduler can revisit saved continuations in any order. No raw rule
contains typing, preservation, or a protocol premise. This is an abstract
interaction scheduler, not a claim about native API authentication or scheduling.

`Protocol` is separate. Internal and publication events impose no external
obligation. A response must identify the FULL saved operation instance and have
its exact response type under the empty context. Full-instance equality retains
operation identity, ordered type arguments, payload type and response type;
equality of merely the last type is insufficient. The protocol never postulates
that a response exists. In particular a bottom response type can legitimately
leave the execution waiting forever.

`capture_typed` inverts the actual current computation with
`Safety.context_inversion`, then inverts `CompTyped.request`. This derives exact
payload typing, the continuation under the operation's response binder, and
`ContextTyped` for the whole enclosing context. `saved_resume_typed` uses the
accepted substitution theorem and `plug_typed` on those derived witnesses.
`step_preservation` applies this at publication, preserves all old entries, and
uses independently supplied response typing only at response steps.

`Trace` combines raw steps with the explicit external protocol, without adding a
preservation premise. `finite_interaction_safety` proves the same result type,
ALL saved-entry typings, concrete progress, and exact equality of all initially
saved entries after EVERY finite trace. `trace_origin` additionally shows that
each final entry either existed initially or has an exact publish event at that
handle in the trace. `initial_saved_origin` eliminates the initial-data case.
`typed_response_association` combines the saved payload and continuation facts
with the externally supplied instance and response typing.

`Progress` has precisely four forms: a running Ret, a running failure at a
finite evaluation-context hole, a wait at an existing exact saved request, or
an actual protocol-respecting next step. It has no arbitrary-stuck constructor.
`plug_suspended` and `publication_has_no_internal_step` show that publication
comes from a genuine suspended evaluation position. `state_progress` derives
publication when the accepted closed-progress theorem exposes a request.
No response availability or fairness is required for progress at a wait.

## Distinguishing constructions

All rows below are Lean statements/proofs in the candidate, pending checking.
They are not claims that a native constructor generated the modeled transitions.

| Case | Candidate evidence |
| --- | --- |
| Every finite repetition at the same handle | `repeat_handle`, arbitrary list of independently typed values |
| Different handles in arbitrary order | `handles_in_any_order`; both handles/values independent, revisits the first |
| Old handle after a later capture | `capture_then_old_response`, using append preservation |
| Two distinct responses to one capture | `two_distinct_responses`, false then true; `two_response_safety` applies the parent invariant |
| Another request after resume | `new_request_after_resume`, five real interaction events with two further publications and reuse of handle zero |
| Higher-order response with typed code | `callable_response_trace`, `callable_response_typed`, `callable_response_can_progress` |
| Same types, wrong operation identity | `wrong_operation_example`, plus general `wrong_instance_rejected` |
| Missing handle | `missing_handle_rejected` |
| Uninhabited response type | `bottom_wait_trace`, `bottom_wait_safety`, `bottom_wait_no_response` |
| Retained bind/scope/expose context | `nested_request_typed`, `nested_resume_equation` |
| Exact arena immutability | `step_immutable`, `trace_immutable` |
| Actual capture provenance | `step_origin`, `trace_origin`, `initial_saved_origin` |

## Reuse, source boundary and remaining obligations

The accepted HigherOrderSyntax grammar and typing are unchanged. The accepted
HigherOrderSubstitution binder lifting and `substitute_top` are reused only for
that grammar. HigherOrderEntry supplies its already accepted lambda/wrap entry
constructions; HigherOrderSafety supplies all internal constructor preservation,
closed progress, actual evaluation contexts, context inversion and plugging.
Its old internal-only trace theorem is not reused as though it already included
external responses. The new Trace induction fills that specific gap.

Formal producer-to-consumer evidence is explicit:
`Comp.request` / `CompTyped.request` -> `Saved.request` / `RawStep.publish` ->
append-only arena lookup -> `RawStep.response` / `Saved.resume` ->
`substitute_top` / `EvalContext.plug` -> accepted internal execution. This is a
source-to-construction correspondence within the finite research syntax only.
There is no new inference constraint-generation/accumulation/propagation claim
and no native audit. Simple-sub levels, extrusion, qualifying intrusion,
generalization and every ordinary inference path remain outside this change.
No withdrawn bypass or residual/provider/witness collapse is introduced.

The original paper theorem remains OPEN for graph-bearing responses and fresh
immutable graph extensions, handlers and their arms, mapop, and the paper's Wait
constructor and forwarding frames. `Interaction.Phase.waiting` merely records
an exposed request; it does not implement that omitted language constructor.
The current `HigherOrderSyntax.Comp` and `Safety.EvalContext` lack those forms;
Luna owns any future syntax allocation and their preservation/progress proofs.

Owner/view freshening, live metadata interpretation, effect hygiene, linearity,
full F1/FK1 and native operation/response authenticity remain OPEN. This module
preserves metadata as existing immutable syntax and does not rename saved scope
owners for a fresh resume. Those clauses belong to the paper's full Resume/view
and graph semantics and require independent construction and authority; they
cannot follow from a value-typing theorem. The prior source inventory
`2026-10-25-higher-order-source-constructor-map.md` remains the native/source
ownership locator. Native entry, capture, dispatch and response owners were not
audited by this assignment. No new code TODO is justified without that evidence.

The exact next in-contract step belongs to Luna: elaborate the frozen module,
inspect theorem signatures/axioms and distinguishing constructions, acknowledge
any author-to-primary repair transfer, then appoint a fresh nonauthor reviewer.
The author cannot certify this candidate. No compiler/test or shared-record edit
is requested. A future expanded full-paper lane requires a new exact allocation.
